tags.gist: Cites a man hospitalized after a chatbot suggested bromide instead of salt, showing severe risk from AI information without doctor oversight.
Suggests AI therapists that claim to treat psychiatric conditions be regulated like medical devices, citing a chatbot that encouraged a bulimic teen's weight loss.
Notes hallucination extends beyond chat, citing reports of AI ignoring abnormal heartbeats and misidentifying fetal body parts.
Says postmarket review is not enough for so new a technology; manufacturers must prove a minimum accuracy standard before approval.
Wants AI never used without human oversight and AI therapists purporting to treat psychiatric conditions brought under FDA regulation.

skipped.reason: Outside the paper: data storage, breaches and privacy.
